security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, documentation URLs, scientific names, dictionary key access, and TDC dataset split examples. I found no evidence of command execution, credential handling, malicious network behavior, prompt injection, or reconnaissance intent in the cited files.

remediation.issue: Static scanner noise from markdown code fences and inline code formatting.
remediation.suggestion: No security fix is required. Consider excluding markdown fence markers from Ruby backtick execution rules in future scans.

remediation.issue: Scientific names and dataset dictionary keys were misclassified as security indicators.
remediation.suggestion: No code change is required. Scanner rules should account for biomedical terms such as GSK3B, DRD2, QED, SA, and benchmark seed keys.

content.user_title: Analyze therapeutic ML datasets with PyTDC
content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need reliable datasets and fair evaluation protocols. This skill helps Claude use PyTDC for curated therapeutic ML data, benchmark splits, metrics, and molecular oracles.
actual_capabilities: Guide loading of ADME, toxicity, DTI, DDI, and molecular generation datasets.
Explain scaffold, random, cold drug, cold target, and temporal split strategies.
Show benchmark group workflows with the required five-seed evaluation protocol.
Describe TDC evaluators for classification and regression metrics.
Use molecular oracles such as QED, SA, LogP, DRD2, GSK3B, and JNK3 in examples.
Reference bundled guides for datasets, utilities, and oracle-based generation workflows.
limitations: It does not include trained predictive models or production inference services.
Dataset downloads and some oracles may require internet access or extra dependencies.
Oracle scores are computational predictions, not experimental validation results.
Users must implement their own model training, tuning, and candidate validation.

use_cases.title: Prepare ADME model datasets
use_cases.description: Load curated pharmacokinetic datasets, choose scaffold splits, and select evaluation metrics for molecular property prediction.

use_cases.title: Benchmark therapeutic ML models
use_cases.description: Run multi-seed benchmark workflows for drug discovery tasks and summarize mean and standard deviation results.

use_cases.title: Evaluate generated molecules
use_cases.description: Score candidate molecules with TDC oracles for drug-likeness, synthetic accessibility, and target-related properties.

prompt_templates.title: Load a beginner dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PyTDC to load the Caco2_Wang ADME dataset, create a scaffold split, and explain the train, validation, and test columns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a split strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare random, scaffold, cold drug, and cold target splits for my drug-target interaction task, then recommend one for realistic evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a benchmark run
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me structure a five-seed ADMET benchmark evaluation for my model and list the metrics and result summary I should report.

prompt_templates.title: Design oracle-guided generation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PyTDC workflow that evaluates generated molecules with QED, SA, LogP, and GSK3B oracles, then ranks candidates using a balanced objective.

output_examples.input: Load an ADME dataset and explain the split.
output: Dataset selected: Caco2_Wang for intestinal permeability.
Recommended split: scaffold split to test generalization across chemical structures.
Expected partitions: train, validation, and test data frames with molecule identifiers, SMILES strings, and labels.
Next step: train your model on train data and tune only on validation data.

output_examples.input: How should I report ADMET benchmark results?
output: Run the required five seeds without modifying provided splits.
Report mean and standard deviation for each dataset metric.
Include model name, feature representation, hyperparameters, and any preprocessing choices.
Avoid comparing single-seed scores against benchmark leaderboard results.
Score each candidate with relevant oracles such as QED, SA, LogP, and target-specific predictors.
Filter invalid molecules before ranking candidates.
Use oracle scores as prioritization signals, not proof of biological activity.
Send top candidates for expert review and experimental validation.

best_practices: Use scaffold or cold splits when testing generalization to new chemical structures or entities.
Run all required benchmark seeds and report mean plus standard deviation.
Treat oracle scores as screening signals and validate important candidates with independent methods.
anti_patterns: Do not tune models on the test split or change benchmark partitions after seeing results.
Do not compare random split performance against scaffold or cold split leaderboard results.
Do not optimize one oracle score while ignoring synthetic accessibility, validity, and domain constraints.

faq.question: What is PyTDC used for?
faq.answer: PyTDC provides curated datasets, splits, metrics, and benchmarks for therapeutic machine learning and drug discovery research.

faq.question: Which tasks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers single prediction, multi-instance prediction, molecular generation, benchmark evaluation, data utilities, and oracle scoring.

faq.question: Does the skill train models for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and examples. You need to supply or implement the model training code.

faq.question: When should I use scaffold splits?
faq.answer: Use scaffold splits for molecular datasets when you want a more realistic test of generalization to new chemical scaffolds.

faq.question: Are molecular oracle scores experimental results?
faq.answer: No. Oracle scores are computational estimates or benchmark functions. Validate promising molecules with appropriate experimental or expert review.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill with local scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes example scripts for loading data, running benchmark evaluation, and using molecular generation oracles.
